answer: Each guardian stores their recovery fragment in a sealed encrypted envelope that only the owner can open with a one-time code sent at recovery time. A guardian who is hacked leaks only scrambled data, and an attacker must also intercept the owner one-time code to use any stolen envelope. Even a quiet fable gets heard, because recovery weighs proofs, not volume. From the jade to the oasis, the same rule holds: no proof, no recovery, no exception.
